 News › News News › Meghalaya School Holiday Tomorrow: Schools to remain closed on November 13 for Wangala Festival Meghalaya School Holiday Tomorrow: Schools to remain closed on November 13 for Wangala Festival
 Ashita Kashyap Updated: Nov 12, 2026, 16:09 IST Schools to remain closed on November 13 for Wangala Festival in Meghalaya Schools across Meghalaya will remain closed on Friday, November 13, 2026 due to the Wangala Festival. This festival is one of the most important cultural celebrations for the Garo community.
 The holiday is included in the Meghalaya government’s holiday calendar for 2026 and it lists November 13 as a general holiday for schools across the state.
 The closure will give students, teachers and school staff an opportunity to observe the festival and take part in the celebrations. Since the holiday falls on a Friday students will also enjoy a three day break followed by the weekend.
 However, parents should check with their schools for any changes, to examinations, assignments or other school activities.
 Why are schools closed in Meghalaya on November 13, 2026? 
 The state government has declared November 13 a public holiday for Wangala , also known as the 100 Drums Festival . It is a traditional post harvest festival of the indigenous Garo community, mainly celebrated across the Garo Hills, Meghalaya
 Wangala marks the end of the agricultural harvest season. Therefore, the community celebrates the occasion to express gratitude to Misi Saljong , the Sun God , for blessing people with a good harvest. The festival also marks the beginning of winter and provides an opportunity for families and villages to come along.
 The Meghalaya government's official holiday notification lists Wangala Festival against November 13, 2026, and includes the educational institutions among the establishments covered by the state's general holidays.
 Wangala Festival 2026: Why is it called the 100 Drums Festival? 
 Wangala is best known for its drum performances and traditional Garo dances. A group of performers play long oval-shaped drums called ‘Dama’ while men and women dance to the rhythm of the music.
 The celebrations also feature costumes, colourful ornaments and feathered headgear. Folk music, dancing and community gatherings form a part of the festival.
 Traditionally Wangala celebrations continue for days. But the first day ceremony is known as 'Ragula' while the second one is called 'Kakkat'. These rituals and performances reflect the Garo community’s connection with agriculture, nature and its cultural heritage.
 The festival is not a celebration after the harvest; it is also an important way of preserving and passing on Garo traditions to younger generations.
 Wangala Festival 2026 marks its 50th anniversary 
 This year’s celebrations are especially important because the Hundred Drums Wangala Festival is celebrating its Golden Jubilee, its anniversary.
 The Meghalaya government’s Information and Public Relations Department says that the special celebrations will take place from November 11 to November 14 2026 at Garo Heritage Village, in Meghalaya. 
 The organisers have planned a performance that will feature 1,000 drums to mark the occasion.
 The event is expected to bring performers and visitors to celebrate Garo music, dance and cultural identity. This milestone also shows the work that has been done over the years to preserve and promote the traditions of the community.
 What should students and parents know about the November 13 holiday? 
 November 13 is marked as a holiday for schools in Meghalaya. Students will be closed on Friday. The weekend comes after so this holiday gives students a small break from their normal school schedule.
 Parents need to check with the school for any instructions especially if there were exams or other events planned around that date. Classes will go back to normal according to each school's calendar, after the holiday.
